name: Author tested components (tests as data on the node)
desc: Carry every interactive component's tests as DATA on the node, the same way you author its behavior/motion/analytics — so a component and the tests that pin it travel together in the graph instead of drifting apart in a parallel file tree.
body:
Author every INTERACTIVE component with a `tests` manifest — the per-node verification CONTRACT, the sibling of the behavior/motion/analytics a component already carries (#3878). The point: a test is DATA on the component, so it travels WITH the node — through a snapshot, a harvest, or a re-seed — instead of living in a parallel file tree that silently drifts out of sync with the thing it pins.
1. If a component is interactive — it exposes an action/event prop the user can trigger (`onClick`, `onChange`, `onSelect`, …) — it MUST declare at least one test. `bsc ui doctor` flags an interactive component with no tests as `no-tests`.
2. Declare each test as `{ name, src }`: `name` is the behavior in plain words (`"calls onSelect with the clicked row"`), `src` is the test body. Name the BEHAVIOR, never the implementation — a test named for the behavior survives a rewrite of the component's internals.
3. Test what the user ACTS on. Every action prop the component declares should be exercised by at least one test: fire it, assert the callback ran with the right argument. A prop no test ever fires is the same smell `unwired-prop` reports.
4. Cover the states the component can be IN, not just its happy path — empty, loading, and error renders are declared behavior (see the `no-empty-state` / `no-loading-state` findings) and each deserves a test.
5. Keep a test self-contained: it may use the component's own props and the kit it is authored against, and nothing else. A test that reaches for app state, the network, or a sibling module is not portable with the node and will not survive a re-seed.
6. Display-only / layout components (no action prop) don't need tests to satisfy the check — but a non-trivial render (a computed label, a conditional branch) is still worth pinning.
When authoring or editing an interactive component, add or update its `tests` in the same pass — never after — and run `bsc ui doctor` to confirm no `no-tests` finding remains.
